text: fixed Two-sided formula response ~ fixed_effects. universal entry's model slot: accepts ASReml fixed form (paired random / rcov) brms / lme4-style bar-grouped formula response ~ x + (1 | g) (case grouping lives formula random / rcov must left NULL). grammar detected call shape; use syntax force . random One-sided formula: ~ random_terms using ASReml syntax. Supports vm(), (), us(), fa(), ar1(), spl(), ped(), dsum(), id(), nested colon terms. rcov One-sided formula: ~ residual_structure. Default ~ units (iid residuals). Use ~ (env):units heterogeneous variance. data data.frame containing variables referenced formulas. family Character: "gaussian", "binomial", "poisson", "negative_binomial", "gamma", "beta". link Character NULL: override default link function (e.g., "probit" binomial). known_matrices Named list matrices referred random formula (e.g., list(Gmat = G_mat, Amat = A_mat)). carrier declared fb_cov() constructor inside random term: dense covariance (vm(group, cov = fb_cov(G, type = "dense"))), user-supplied lower-triangular Cholesky factor (vm(group, cov = fb_cov(L, type = "chol")); greta backend ), sparse precision matrix Matrix::dgCMatrix (vm(group, cov = fb_cov(Q, type = "precision")); greta INLA backends). bare dense forms vm(group, V = ...) / ped(group, = ...) remain default; legacy v0.3.7 keyword carriers (chol = , precision = , blocks = , low_rank_factor = ) deprecated emit migration warning. See structured-covariance vignette per-type worked examples. weights Optional numeric weight vector (length N); sets Var = sigma^2 / w. n_samples Integer: number posterior samples per chain. warmup Integer: number warmup (burn-) iterations per chain. chains Integer: number MCMC chains. prior optional fb_prior() object specifying priors via PC-canonical hybrid DSL (preferred). supplied overrides prior_vc_sd variance components covers. See fb_prior(). prior_fixed_sd Numeric: SD fixed-effect normal priors, applied uniformly intercept, factor contrasts, continuous slopes, factor x continuous interactions, ()-expression terms. Default 100 — weakly informative natural response scale vast majority agricultural / clinical responses (covers responses central tendency several hundred without crushing posterior toward zero), still regularising sample sizes ~ 30 per coefficient. Set wider (e.g. 1000) responses larger natural scale, narrower explicit shrinkage. Rationale follows Gelman (2006) Bayesian Analysis 1(3):515-534 weakly-informative priors regression coefficients data scale. prior_vc_sd Numeric: hyperparameter legacy lognormal(0, prior_vc_sd) variance-component prior. Note: prior prior_vc_sd left defaults, v0.1 activates bounded-uniform default SD scale (uniform(0, U) family-aware U: 5 * sd(y) Gaussian; 5 logit scale binomial / beta; 3 log scale Poisson / negative-binomial / gamma) sigma every named random-effect group. Theory: Gelman (2006), Bayesian Analysis 1(3):515-534. legacy lognormal(0, 1) default fires prior_vc_sd passed explicitly. Silence one-time announcement message via options(flexyBayes.silence_default_prior_note = TRUE). verbose Logical: print generated greta code console. mcmc_verbose Logical: show MCMC progress bar greta. return_code Logical: TRUE, return generated code string without fitting model. review_code Logical: TRUE, fit model immediately; instead return <flexybayes_review> deferred-execution object carrying generated backend code, resolved prior, parsed intermediate representation (IR), captured call, snapshot .Random.seed. Inspect code cat_code(); run deferred fit proceed(); second proceed() call returns cached fit. Useful teaching / auditing surface long MCMC run. Default FALSE preserves existing run-immediately semantics. session-level override available via options(flexyBayes.review_code_default = TRUE); argument value call time always wins. Closest published precedent: brms::make_stancode() plus chains = 0 idiom "everything except sampling". review_code = TRUE return_code = TRUE mutually exclusive. backend Character: one "auto" (default), "greta", "inla", "brms". "auto" call consults lgm_gate() routes INLA model latent-Gaussian feasible (deterministic faster certified class), greta (full MCMC, universal fallback) otherwise — -backend call reaches every available engine model supports. "greta" forces full MCMC; "inla" forces INLA raises structured refusal model LGM-feasible; "brms" Stan passthrough via brms (refuses asreml structured-covariance terms — vm/ped/fa/us/ar1 — lossless Stan translation). "auto", falling back greta (gate refusal, INLA installed, INLA numerical failure) emits one-time silenceable note; options(flexyBayes.silence_auto_fallback_note = TRUE) silences gate-refusal / numerical-fallback note options(flexyBayes.silence_auto_inla_missing_note = TRUE) INLA--installed note. backend_decision() surfaces full dispatch trace (including rejected_routes) post-fit. return_code = TRUE review_code = TRUE requested "auto", call resolves greta (code-producing engine); explicit backend = "inla" review_code = TRUE raises structured refusal INLA-side code-slot support lands. aggregate One "auto" (default), TRUE, FALSE. Exact sufficient-statistics aggregation gate. "auto" consults aggregation plan routes per-cell emit path IR scope (gaussian-identity, binomial-logit, poisson-log; fixed + random-intercept; productive compression) backend = "inla"; backend = "greta", "auto" falls per-row path even plan eligible (TRUE required activate greta aggregated emit explicitly). TRUE forces aggregation either backend – raises structured refusal plan declares ineligibility. FALSE skips gate entirely. Aggregated fits carry $exactness == "aggregated_exact" dispatch trace's path slot reads "aggregated_gaussian" (gaussian) "aggregated_count" (binomial / poisson). --core datasets fit memory, see flexybayes_stream(). asymmetry documented behaviour rather bug: greta uses dense-matrix per-row emit default predictable RAM, switching aggregated path silently change posterior numerical profile without explicit opt-. plan Logical: TRUE, short-circuit intermediate representation (IR) build return <fb_plan> object carrying IR, routing decision, representation plan, aggregation plan, prediction plan, without emitting backend code fitting.  Equivalent calling fb_plan() formula triple — exposed inline flexybayes(plan = TRUE) users can reach planning object without re-typing call.  Default FALSE preserves run- immediately semantics.  Mutually exclusive return_code review_code. syntax One "auto" (default), "asreml", "brms", "greta". Selects fixed interpreted. "auto" detects grammar call shape (bar-grouped formula read brms, otherwise ASReml); values force grammar. "greta" (native greta_model) reserved: pass models fb_greta() v0.4.x; direct ingest universal entry lands v0.5.0.

title: Predict from a flexybayes model — predict.flexybayes
text: object flexybayes object newdata Optional new data frame prediction. NULL, returns fitted values original data. type "link" linear predictor, "response" response scale. se.fit Logical: return standard errors? chunk_size Optional integer. supplied, newdata rows chunk_size, prediction iterates chunks size concatenates results. Default NULL preserves single-pass behaviour. Per-chunk prediction uses factor-level dictionary chunk_size change numerical output – wall-time peak memory profile. typical setting large newdata chunk_size = 10000L. allow_new_levels One "population" (default), "sample", "refuse". Policy handling factor levels newdata fit-time dictionary. "population" sets unknown-level rows NA affected column emits warning naming count; downstream prediction returns NA rows. "refuse" raises structured stop first unknown level. "sample" (active since v0.3.5) layers fresh Normal(0, tau_<group>) random-effect realisation onto unknown row per posterior draw – caller's set.seed() controls reproducibility. -memory return reports posterior-mean prediction (sampled-RE contribution averages toward zero across draws); file-backed return (output_file = ...) captures proper per-row posterior interval reflecting sampled-RE uncertainty. consulted fit carries extras$fb_dataset slot (fits produced v0.3.4+); legacy fits skip dictionary resolution entirely. output_file Optional character path. supplied, prediction written disk format resolved format. file tabular structure columns point, lower, upper (95\ columns newdata. Refuses output_file already exists (silent overwrite). Returns path invisibly. Requires fit posterior draws $greta$draws (greta-backend fits including fb_brms(..., backend = "greta")); INLA fits currently expose per-draw access route structured refusal. Default NULL (-memory return). format One "auto" (default), "csv", "rds", "fst". consulted output_file supplied. "auto" resolves : "csv" interop = TRUE; "fst" nrow(newdata) >= 1e6 fst installed; "rds" otherwise. "fst" requested without fst installed raises structured refusal naming install command. fst path 30–40x faster rds N >= 1e6 per Stage-3B-shape benchmark (benchmark_results/fst_stage3b_2026-05-23). interop Logical. TRUE, format-resolution rule format = "auto" prefers "csv" (universally readable) rds / fst (R-/ fst-). Useful handing prediction grid non-R consumer. Default FALSE. consulted output_file supplied format = "auto". ... Additional arguments (ignored)

title: Cross-engine posterior triangulation — triangulate
text: fit_a fit object fb_as_draws_simple method (e.g., flexybayes greta, flexybayes_inla INLA). fit_b second fit object, typically different backend. name_map named character vector list mapping fit_b's parameter names (left) canonical names matching fit_a (right). Optional. transform_a, transform_b named list functions, taking numeric vector posterior draws returning numeric vector length. Names key parameters fit_a / fit_b (using fit's original parameter names). Common use: pass transform_b = list("Precision g" = function(x) 1 / sqrt(x)) convert INLA's precision draws standard-deviation scale line greta's sigma_g. Optional. n_samples integer: number posterior samples draw fits whose extractor needs sampling (e.g., INLA via INLA::inla.posterior.sample).

title: Cross-engine posterior triangulation — triangulate
text: parameter present fits (post name_map), returned table reports: posterior means, posterior SDs, Q2.5 / Q97.5 differences (tail drift), Wasserstein-1 distance (1D empirical), SD ratio, R-hat--means scalar compares -engine vs within-engine variance. Parameters present one fit reported only_a / only_b. Backends use different parameter naming conventions; supply name_map = c(<fit_b name> = <canonical name>, ...) align . Without alignment, literal-match parameter names compared. Backends also use different parameter scales variance components – INLA reports precision (Precision g), greta reports standard deviation (sigma_g). Supply transform_a / transform_b – named lists one-argument functions keyed parameter name – put two posteriors common scale comparison. Transforms applied first; name_map aligns (already-transformed) fit_b names fit_a's canonical names. Names transform_b therefore refer fit_b's original parameter names, post-name_map canonical names.

title: Cross-engine posterior triangulation — triangulate
text: one inputs aggregated-gaussian fit (cell-level sufficient statistics rather per-row likelihood), posteriors compared directly comparable two fits share priors. aggregated path combines cell-mean likelihood precision prior carrying closed-form correction absorbs within-cell sum--squares; default prior recovers per-row posterior numerical precision, aggregated fit tagged prior_parametrization = "per_row_equivalent" (visible aggregated print() / summary() canonical_names()). explicit prior supplied fit tagged "custom": equivalence default-prior per-row fit longer holds, aggregated INLA path observation-precision prior plumbed , custom residual prior silently applied . reading agreement metrics custom-prior aggregated fit, confirm inputs carry prior prior_summary().

title: Cross-engine posterior triangulation — triangulate
code: # Live INLA posterior sampling can fail in restricted-process # check environments (the `inla.posterior.sample` parallelism # check trips); the example uses `\dontrun{}` deliberately. On # an interactive install with greta + INLA + sn available it # runs in a few seconds. if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ if (requireNamespace("greta", quietly = TRUE) &&     requireNamespace("INLA",  quietly = TRUE)) {   set.seed(1)   d <- data.frame(y = rnorm(40), x = rnorm(40),                   g = factor(rep(1:5, 8)))   fit_g <- fb(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = d, backend = "greta",               n_samples = 100, warmup = 100, chains = 1,               verbose = FALSE)   fit_i <- fb(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = d, backend = "inla",               verbose = FALSE)   prec_to_sd <- function(x) 1 / sqrt(x)   tri <- triangulate(     fit_g, fit_i,     transform_b = list(       "Precision for g"                         = prec_to_sd,       "Precision for the Gaussian observations" = prec_to_sd     ),     name_map = c(       "(Intercept):1"                           = "mu_atg",       "x:1"                                     = "beta_x",       "Precision for g"                         = "sigma_g",       "Precision for the Gaussian observations" = "sigma_e_atg"     )   )   print(tri) } } # }

Engine pins single-engine, name. fb_greta(), fb_inla(), fb_brms() fit via exactly one engine — fb_<engine>(...) sugar fb(..., backend = "<engine>"). Passing conflicting backend pin now clear error rather silently overridden. fb_brms(backend = "brms") (redundant self-pin) still accepted. fb_brms() longer takes non-brms backend. multi-backend role moved fb() / flexybayes() 0.4.1; 0.5.0 fb_brms() brms engine pin. Pass formula fb() reach greta, inla, auto. fb() / flexybayes() fit native greta model directly. Pass greta::model() object (fb_from_greta() intermediate representation) straight fb(); fit via greta returned full post-fit surface. keep canonical-name map cross-engine triangulate(), build representation reuse : fb(fb_from_greta(model, canonical_names = c(...))). fb_greta(model = ) longer separate native-graph verb. model = argument still works (mapped universal model slot), existing native-graph calls keep fitting; recommended form fb_greta(model) , canonical map, fb_greta(fb_from_greta(model, canonical_names = c(...))).

Previously greta fit plot() method, plot() INLA, brms, aggregated, native-greta fit fell graphics::plot.default() errored. plot(fit, type = "effects") now works backend, plot types need quantities backend expose (trace plots without MCMC draws, residual plots without fitted values) report clearly instead erroring. Positional named prior arguments behave identically. prior written positionally (example normal(0, 50)) now read named form (normal(0, sd = 50)) every emit path; previously positional scale silently dropped default greta INLA paths. predict(), emmeans(), marginaleffects work INLA fit brms-grammar mixed model. model written y ~ x + (1 | g) fitted via INLA previously refused downstream calls, random-effect bar term leaked fixed-effect design matrix. formula() INLA fit now returns fixed-effect formula , documented, design matrix matches fitted coefficients. Aggregated INLA fits covered . non-binary binomial response refused greta backend rather silently fitted Bernoulli model. text: triangulate(fit_a, fit_b) computes mean difference, SD ratio, tail drift, Wasserstein-1, R-hat--means every parameter two fits common. Canonical-name resolution (see ) means caller usually need pass name_map.

title: flexyBayes 0.2.0 (development)
text: backend names parameters differently (greta’s sigma_g, INLA’s Precision g precision scale, brms’s sd_g__Intercept, etc.). canonical_names() resolves backend-native names single canonical name applies appropriate scale transform — visibly, INLA’s precision draws flipped SD scale comparison. triangulate() uses registry align parameters computing metrics.
code: canonical_names(fit_i) #>   native                canonical    transform #>   "(Intercept)"         "(Intercept)" identity #>   "Precision for g"     "sd_g"        1/sqrt(.) #>   "Precision for the Gaussian observations" "sigma" 1/sqrt(.)

title: flexyBayes 0.2.0 (development)
text: new exported S3 generic surfaces resolved priors used fit model. summary distinguishes three resolution paths: auto-default — bounded uniform SD per Gelman (2006); fires neither user fb_prior() legacy prior_vc_sd scalar supplied. user-supplied — fb_prior() object caller passed via prior argument. legacy-scalar — prior_fixed_sd / prior_vc_sd bridge, preserved verbatim prior_vc_sd passed explicitly. fb_greta() fits summary flagged declaration_only = TRUE flexyBayes re-prior user-built greta graph; prior records user declared model encodes.
code: fit <- flexybayes(Reaction ~ Days, random = ~ Subject,                   data = sleepstudy) prior_summary(fit) #> <prior_summary>  backend = greta #>   Source: auto-default bounded uniform on SD (Gelman 2006) #>     Upper bound U = 282.7 #>     Scale basis    = 5 * sd(Reaction)

title: flexyBayes 0.2.0 (development)
text: new optional argument flexybayes(), fb_brms(), fb_greta() lets users inspect generated backend code sampling fires, advance fit ready: returned <flexybayes_review> object carries generated code, parsed IR, resolved prior, captured call, snapshot .Random.seed. seed snapshot restored proceed() entry direct call review--proceed pair reproduce R-RNG state. review_code = TRUE return_code = TRUE (older code-string-option) mutually exclusive. Default FALSE; session-level override via options(flexyBayes.review_code_default = TRUE).
code: rev <- flexybayes(yield ~ env, random = ~ geno, data = trial,                   review_code = TRUE) rev                  # two-line summary: backend + IR dimensions cat_code(rev)        # emit the generated greta (or Stan) code fit <- proceed(rev)  # fit; a second proceed(rev) returns the cache

title: flexyBayes 0.2.0 (development)
text: Auto-default (prior prior_vc_sd supplied): Structured-covariance random terms (vm, ped, , us, fa, ar1) currently fall back legacy lognormal(0, prior_vc_sd) default; per-form uniform defaults scheduled v0.2.5. PC prior remains first-class explicit option via fb_prior(sigma ~ pc(upper = U, prob = p)) cross-engine interlingua (Simpson et al. 2017) translation across greta / INLA / brms. prior_fixed_sd default raised 10 100 cycle; previous value tight responses natural data scale (e.g., sleepstudy$Reaction mean ≈ 298 ms) induced substantial intercept bias REML reference. fb_prior() accepts targets sigma, sd(group), b(name), cor(group), smooth(var), families pc, normal, student_t, half_normal, half_cauchy, cauchy, gamma, exponential, lkj, uniform.
